questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Italy

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was okay easy but be aware that Italian bureaucracy has its challenges!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a welcome letter and then I had to show up at an office to register. Besides that, not much information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It had its challenges as you have to find private housing in Milano. I would recommend the site DoveVivo.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Is is VERY expensive. The average cost for a room is around 800 euro.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to show up at the international offices to then register in person. fairly easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were able to write to the international office whenever. They had quite quick response time so that was nice.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite succesful. Most of the classes I registered for, I got. During my stay I changed one of my courses for another - this was a very easy process with no problems. Be aware though that it might no be possible to have courses in Milano that aligns with your field of study back home. I had to take courses that was from a completely different type of faculty than the one I study at in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be settled in the fact that you might not be able to find courses that suits your degree.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I (+ the other exchange students I knew) was only able to take MA classes during our stay. Don't be alarmed though - I would say that the level of the courses aligns with danish BA courses. I took courses from completely different faculties than my field of study and I found it quite easy to follow along.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar in the way that it was also "class-teaching" - in the way that we are used to at UCPH. But it was very different in the sense that the way of teaching isnt very interactive; the class goes by with the professor just giving a lecture - no assigns to do in class etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Consumer Culture 
Wars of Images 
Ethnic Relations and Cultural Differences 
Migrations, Diversity and Non-Discrimination

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All in all I would say that all my courses are recommendable. Be aware though that the "Migrations, Diversity and Non-Discrimination"-course is 50% a law course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I wouldnt say that there was any unexpected costs really. But I was very surprised at how expensive rent is in the city.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I expected - as well as rent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm not quite sure as I never engaged in any of them. But I know that the Erasmus programme organized a lot of different stuff for the international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Maybe some of the erasmus oragnized events

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel so other places in Italy. And if you are staying in Milano then on the weekends there are a lot of different flea markets and good museums.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust. Milanese culture is very laissez faire and quite similar to copenhagen in some sense.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The amount of italian people who doesnt speak english.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Italian culture is much more friendly than Danish! people are very open and welcoming towards strangers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Beware of the expensive rent!
Things are quite chaotic in the beginning as you dont receive an abundance of information (+if you come in january as I did, then there are no welcoming events for erasmus - these events only begin mid february!)
Dont choose this destination with a wish for expanding your academic profile; it is very limited how many courses in english that they offer (I'm a humanities student and I had to take courses at their version of CSS)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be quite chaotic at times.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely the people. Firstly there are many danish students going to milano every semester and secondly, people are generally quite welcoming towards exchange students, per my experience, because there are many international students at the university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out the Italian bureaucracy

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
